messages.subject: Defective battery cells - Calderhall - potential claim
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

Following our call, I'm writing to formally instruct Whitfield Carter on the Calderhall matter. As discussed, we bought three module strings of LFP cells from Calderhall Cells Ltd for the Brackmoor 50MW/100MWh project under a Cell Supply Agreement dated 22 May 2024 (total price 2.94m, paid in full). String B failed badly during commissioning in November - accelerated capacity fade, voltage divergence and, worryingly, localised heating that tripped our thermal interlocks twice.

We've had Wraysbury Materials Laboratory investigate and their report (24 January) points squarely at manufacturing defects. Calderhall are blaming our integration, which we don't accept. The commissioning delay has cost us a lot, including LDs we've had to pay our EPC customer.

Can your team take this on? Helena and Nadia (our GC) are copied. Happy to send the agreement, the Wraysbury report and our cost build-up.

Marcus

Marcus Calder | Co-founder & CTO | Verdant Energy Systems

messages.subject: RE: Defective battery cells - Calderhall - potential claim
messages.plaintextBody:
Marcus,

Thank you - yes, we'd be glad to act. I'm copying Tom Gallagher and Elena Marchetti who will work with me on this. On a first read this looks like a strong breach-of-warranty / Sale of Goods claim; the live battleground will be whether the consequential-loss exclusion in the supply agreement knocks out the EPC liquidated damages and lost revenue, so the contemporaneous record of what Calderhall knew about your downstream deadlines will matter.

Please do send the executed supply agreement, the Wraysbury report and your cost build-up. We'll send a short engagement letter today and aim to get a letter before action out within a fortnight.

We'll need to be careful with the affected cells - please preserve them and the BMS data.

Sarah

Sarah Whitfield
Partner | Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
T +44 (0)20 7946 0500
www.whitfieldcarter.com

Confidential and may be legally privileged.
